news.Title: Zacks Industry Outlook Highlights Cisco Systems, Digi International and Lantronix
news.Content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – October 30, 2026 – Today, Zacks Equity Research discusses Cisco Systems CSCO, Digi International DGII and Lantronix LTRX.

Industry: Computer - Networking

Link: https://www.zacks.com/commentary/3017988/3-stocks-to-consider-from-a-flourishing-networking-industry

The Zacks Computer - Networking industry participants are expected to benefit from the networking infrastructure upgrade driven by AI workloads, cloud computing, big data, network security and next-generation connectivity.

The proliferation of AI workloads and hyperscale data centers is accelerating investments in high-speed interconnects, optical networking and Ethernet switches. Players in this space are focused on capitalizing on the multi-billion-dollar AI infrastructure opportunity. Increasing adoption of AI-driven applications across enterprises is also driving investments in next-gen networking infrastructure capable of supporting higher bandwidth, lower latency and heightened security requirements. Continued deployment of 5G, the proliferation of the Internet of Things (IoT), industrial automation and edge computing is strengthening demand for reliable connectivity solutions. Increasing deployment of Wi-Fi 7 also presents a significant growth opportunity.

Also, the explosion of AI workloads requires a major upgrade to observability infrastructure. There is a greater need for continuous monitoring of hybrid environments and tighter security amid rising attacks. This will spur demand for innovative networking products, favoring prospects for prominent industry players such as Cisco Systems , Digi International and Lantronix .

However, cautious IT spending amid heightened uncertainty over global macroeconomic conditions and volatile supply-chain dynamics due to tariff troubles continues to be concerning for the participants in the near term. Fierce competition is an overhang on pricing power and margin expansion.

Industry Description

The Zacks Computer-Networking industry comprises companies that offer networking and Internet-connected products, including wireless (Wi-Fi and Long-Term Evolution or LTE), Ethernet and powerline, focusing on dependability and ease of use. The products are available in numerous configurations to cater to the changing requirements of consumers in each geographic territory where it operates.

Several industry players also provide mission-critical IoT solutions and network security services to help clients build next-generation connected products, and implement and manage critical communications infrastructures in demanding environments with enhanced safety levels. Focus on developing IoT sensors, drones and wearables amid increasing demand for cloud computing-based contact tracing applications is driving the industry.

Story Continues

4 Trends Influencing the Industry's Future

Technological Advancement Opening Business Avenues: The proliferation of generative AI, agentic AI and high adoption of cloud and data-intensive applications is driving higher traffic and creating a need for advanced optical networking, high-speed interconnects, Ethernet switches, routing and wireless infrastructure. The transition toward 800G and 1.6T networking technologies is expected to further drive infrastructure modernization and capacity expansion.

Expansion of industrial IoT and edge computing, and the increasing popularity of smart connected devices are further creating growth opportunities. Rising cybersecurity concerns are emerging as a key tailwind, driving demand for solutions such as threat detection, network monitoring and zero-trust security architectures.

Continued Deployment of 5G to Boost Growth Prospects: The continued expansion of the 5G technology hinges on substantial investments to upgrade infrastructure in the core fiber backhaul network to support growth in data services. Efforts to develop smart connected homes, hospitals, factories, buildings, cities and self-driving vehicles bode well for industry players. These firms invest heavily in LTE, broadband and fiber to provide additional capacity and improve Internet and wireless networks. These initiatives hold promise.

Wi-Fi 7 Upgrade Cycle to Drive Momentum: Brisk technological advancement, dynamic products, high-speed connectivity, low latency and evolving industry standards define the networking industry. The growing clout of the latest Wi-Fi 6E-compliant residential gateways, Wi-Fi routers, set-top boxes and wireless range extenders is a testament to the same.

The increasing demand for connecting more devices to the network has been driving demand for Wi-Fi 6E devices. Wi-Fi 6E addresses Wi-Fi spectrum shortage issues by providing continuous channel bandwidth to support a higher number of connected devices without compromising speed. The rollout of Wi-Fi 7 bodes well for the companies in this space.

Macroeconomic Turmoil Is Concerning: Global macroeconomic weakness and volatile supply-chain dynamics are persistent concerns. Tariff troubles, especially between the United States and China, remain an overhang on global supply chains. Inflation could affect spending across small and medium-sized businesses globally and uncertainty in business visibility could dent the industry's near-term performance.

The computer networking industry remains highly competitive, with a large number of established and new players vying for market share. As growth stabilizes, competition often intensifies, leading to pricing pressure and margin compression.

Zacks Industry Rank Indicates Bright Near-Term Prospects

The Zacks Computer-Networking Industry is housed within the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector. The industry carries a Zacks Industry Rank #75, positioning it in the top 30% of more than 247 Zacks industries.

The group's Zacks Industry Rank, which is the average of the Zacks Rank of all the member stocks, indicates bright near-term prospects. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than two to one.

Before we present a few stocks you may want to consider for your portfolio, considering bright prospects, let us look at the industry's recent stock-market performance and valuation picture

Industry Outperforms the S&P 500 and the Sector

The Zacks Computer-Networking industry has outperformed the S&P 500 composite and the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector in the past year.

The industry has gained 51.9% over this period, compared with the broader sector's 13.4% rally. The S&P 500 has appreciated 13.3% over the same time frame.

Industry's Current Valuation

Based on the forward 12-month price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio, a common multiple for valuing Computer-Networking stocks, the industry is currently trading at 24.62X, compared with the S&P 500's 19.27X. It is also higher than the sector's forward-12-month P/E of 19.25X.

In the past five years, the industry traded as high as 31.47X and as low as 12.45X, with the median being 17.27X.

3 Computer-Networking Stocks to Add to Your Portfolio

Cisco Systems: Headquartered in San Jose, CA, the company offers identity and access, advanced threat and unified threat management solutions.

Cisco is benefiting from the demand for AI Infrastructure solutions, with hyperscaler demand acting as a key catalyst. The company expects AI infrastructure revenues from hyperscalers to reach $7.5 billion in fiscal 2027.

Strong demand for its Silicon One based systems and Acacia optical networking solutions is expected to support growth. Fiscal 2026 hyperscaler AI orders were about 60% Silicon One-based systems and 40% optics. Acacia generated more than $1 billion in orders in the fiscal fourth quarter.

On the last earnings call, CSCO noted that accelerating agentic AI is driving a "networking super cycle" resulting in increasing demand for its Networking stack to support inferencing across cloud, on-premise and edge environments. In October, Cisco announced a collaboration with NVIDIA to develop an open industry specification for next-generation 400G-per-lane pluggable optics, further strengthening its position in the evolving AI networking ecosystem.

For fiscal 2027, Cisco projects revenues of $72.2-$73.4 billion and non-GAAP earnings of $5.05-$5.11 per share. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fiscal 2027 bottom line is pinned at $5.11, unchanged in the past 30 days. Shares have gained 51.3% in the past year.

At present, CSCO carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

Lantronix : Based in Irvine, CA, Lantronix specializes in providing Industrial and Edge AI IoT solutions for high-growth applications in certain verticals, including enterprise IT, smart cities and commercial and defense unmanned systems.

The company's unmanned systems business has emerged as a meaningful growth driver. Revenues from Unmanned systems came in at $12.6 million in fiscal 2026 and management expects the segment to represent 15% to 20% of total revenues in fiscal 2027. Increasing adoption of AI-enabled drones and counter-UAS applications across defense, industrial and commercial applications presents significant opportunities for its unmanned systems business.  The recent inclusion of its Open-Q 8550CS system-on-module in the Blue UAS Framework strengthens its ability to serve U.S. defense drone manufacturers.

The company also introduced the Spotter edge AI computing platform, which expands its offerings for autonomous drones and robotics.

Beyond unmanned systems, the IoT System Solutions is witnessing improving conditions after federal government shutdowns led to extended procurement cycles. The tuck-in acquisition of Vecima Networks' Industrial IoT business, including the Nero Global Tracking platform, is also expanding its recurring software revenue base.

However, tightening memory availability and rising costs remain concerns, while the increasing contribution from relatively lower-margin unmanned systems solutions could weigh on profitability.

At present, LTRX carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fiscal 2027 earnings is 22 cents per share, unchanged in the past 60 days. Shares have gained 23.8% in the past year.

Digi International: Based in Hopkins, MN, Digi is a well-known provider of business and mission-critical Internet of Things (IoT) products and services globally. The company's industrial Internet of Things offerings encompass embedded, edge and turnkey vertical solutions. These solutions find applications across emerging technology trends such as AI, edge computing and industrial automation. The company is embedding AI across its portfolio.

Digi's outlook remains supported by sustained ARR growth, ongoing benefits from acquisitions and the long-term opportunity to integrate AI into industrial IoT solutions. The company expects ARR to grow 27% in fiscal 2026, up from 25% projected earlier.

To capitalize on the AI opportunity, DGII had unveiled DANI, the Digi Artificial Network Intelligence agent, earlier in the year. DANI is an AI network operations agent that is embedded in Digi Remote Manager, a networking device management platform, enabling network operators/managed service providers to monitor issues, identify causes and offer recommended actions through a unified conversational interface.

The recent launch of Digi EX60, an enterprise 5G router integrating Wi-Fi 7 and AI-assisted network management capabilities, further strengthens its offerings for distributed enterprise networks.

Digi continues to pursue strategic acquisitions, which are likely to supplement organic growth. The proposed acquisition of Disruptive Technologies is expected to expand the capabilities and reach of its SmartSense platform. The company expects the transaction to contribute approximately $9 million in additional adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow in fiscal 2028. The transaction is expected to close before the end of 2026, subject to regulatory approval.

On the last earnings call, management highlighted challenges in the supply chain, which could exert pressure on margins.

At present, DGII carries a Zacks Rank #3. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fiscal 2027 bottom line is pegged at $3.17, unchanged in the past 60 days. Shares have gained 106% in the past year.

news.Title: The Case Against a SpaceX and Tesla Merger
news.Content:
While we don't know what terms, if any, are on the table for a potential merger, there's a strong case that now isn't the best time for Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA) to pursue a merger with Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ: SPCX). The argument rests on two main ideas. First, it runs contrary to market trends; second, Tesla is on the cusp of delivering significant shareholder value after years of disappointment.

Different risk and capital profiles

Over the last decade, the major trend with industrial conglomerates such as General Electric, United Technologies Corporation, Honeywell , 3M , Danaher , Johnson Controls , and Emerson Electric has been to break them up. While each company had its own circumstances, three themes apply to all:

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Separating companies allows for greater management and operational focus.

The market has tended to apply a so-called conglomerate discount, and investors increasingly value the ability to make targeted investments.

Each company has its own specific risk and its own capital allocation priorities, and they are better served as stand-alone companies.

Given the incredible complexity inherent in managing Tesla (EVs, robotaxi/Cybercab, Optimus, energy generation/storage, charging infrastructure, and a host of investments in building its own supply chain) and SpaceX (launch services, artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, Starlink, defense networks), it's not hard to see how complex a merged entity would become.

The argument over the conglomerate discount is admittedly subject to change, as conglomerates once commanded a premium. However, that's not the case now, and until it changes, there's no strong reason to believe a merger will lead to an immediate market-valuation rerating of the merged entity. On the contrary, the opposite could occur.

Different risk profiles and capital profiles

The argument from specific risk and capital profiles is the strongest. Tesla is on the cusp of beginning a multiyear journey to scale its robotaxi service and generate a long stream of recurring revenue from robotaxi/Cybercab. Investors can disagree on its profit potential amid competition, but robotaxi/Cybercab is baked into the valuation, and if you are holding the stock, you presumably believe in the potential of autonomous driving.

Story Continues

While it will obviously require significant upfront capital investment to build out the network, Tesla has the resources to do so and create a company with significant long-term cash flows. The same argument, albeit a few more years out, applies to Optimus. Tesla does not need SpaceX to achieve its own goals.

In contrast, SpaceX operates in a high-risk sector that requires even more massive capital investment. Moreover, while Starlink is currently SpaceX's profit generator, its revenue driver is the Super Intelligence business. The former is effectively funding growth in the latter.

Tesla is moving toward becoming a company with a long-term stream of recurring revenue, scaling robotaxi/Cybercab and, in time, Optimus, and a play on physical AI. In contrast, SpaceX is a business that requires massive, ongoing, and uncertain capital expenditures and is a play on AI infrastructure.

Regarding the uncertainty of capital expenditures, consider orbital data centers and SpaceX. Their depreciation rate is likely to be high because they realistically can't be serviced in space and, unlike terrestrial data centers, which can replace servers and chips, will likely last only as long as their graphics processing units (GPUs) remain useful. A high depreciation rate implies higher maintenance capital spending.

Tesla hasn't released value from robotaxi/Cybercab yet

To understand this argument, consider how private equity might run Tesla. Their typical model is to generate value from the investment and sell the asset only once the business is firing on all cylinders, and it can optimize the price.

If you believe Tesla will evolve into a company generating billions of recurring revenue from its Cybercab fleet and then from Optimus, it makes sense to hold the asset, at least until the company proves the doubters wrong and releases value from the robotaxi rollout. At which point, Tesla shareholders will be in a stronger position to demand a healthier premium for the business.

What it means to investors

Again, while it's true that we don't know what kind of offer or what deal it will be, or even if there will be a proposal at all, the reality is the value of Tesla will key off of its current market price, and if you think it's undervalued and/or want to wait until the company releases value from robotaxi, then an offer now is unlikely to lead to a favorable outcome for you.

All told, in a merger, Tesla investors would dilute their claim on cash flows from robotaxi, EVs, and robotics (physical AI) in favor of using that cash to support space exploration and cloud computing (AI infrastructure). This creates a merged company with a significantly different risk and capital-allocation profile from Tesla, and they might not get full value for their Tesla shares until robotaxi scales.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger

Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005.

But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout, a massive technology build-out that Google's CEO says could be more profound than fire or electricity.

While everyone watches the chip designers, one "backbone" company provides the critical technology that Nvidia and AMD literally cannot function without. We've detailed this under-the-radar player in our new AI Playbook.

Silicon Motion Technology Corp ( NASDAQ:SIMO ) delivered record Q3 2026 revenue of $560 million, up 24% sequentially and 131% year-over-year, exceeding guidance.

A : CFO Jason Tsai attributed the outlook to significant traction in MonTitan enterprise SSD controllers and aggressive ramping of Ferri automotive solutions, which are multi-year engagements with long product cycles. He noted that based on backlog and anticipated growth from Titan, SSD controllers, and Ferri automotive, the company believes it can sustain low-to-mid 50% gross margins.

Q : Can you discuss the near-CPU boot drive opportunity with DRAM, including the size of the market and the ramp timeline? A : CEO Wallace Kou stated that NAND makers are deprioritizing low-capacity near-CPU boot drives (1TB-2TB) as they focus on high-capacity SSDs, creating a significant shortage. He estimates this market will reach at least $10 billion by 2030. Silicon Motion expects firmware and solutions ready by early Q1 2027, with production ramping in the second half of 2027, leveraging its existing controller technology with built-in OCP features.

Q : How is Silicon Motion positioned with wafer supply, packaging, and test capacity to support 40% growth next year, and is there upside potential? A : CEO Wallace Kou acknowledged industry-wide shortages across substrates, materials, wafers, NAND, and test capacity. However, he stated the manufacturing team secured 2027 wafer supply primarily with TSMC, along with test capacity, assembly capacity, and substrate materials. He expressed confidence in supporting at least 40% year-over-year growth, with more detailed 2027 guidance to come next quarter.

Q : As the SSD solution business grows to over 40% of revenue, how do you manage NAND pricing exposure, particularly if NAND prices decline? A : CEO Wallace Kou explained that Silicon Motion negotiates six-month pricing contracts with customers, passing through NAND cost increases while maintaining margin protection. He expects NAND price increases to moderate as spot prices become challenging for module makers. CFO Jason Tsai added that if NAND availability and pricing improve, customers would likely double density, and re-specing to normal specs plus new customer opportunities position the company to grow even as the NAND market stabilizes.

Q : What is the revenue mix between solutions (Ferri, Boot Drive, automotive) and controllers, and how will it change next year? A : CEO Wallace Kou stated that approximately 40% of total revenue came from solutions (boot drive, automotive) and 60% from controllers in Q3. He expects the mix to become more balanced at roughly 50/50 next year as automotive solutions grow.

Q : With enterprise and Ferri becoming a larger portion of the business, should we expect consumer seasonality from Q4 to Q1 to diminish? A : CFO Jason Tsai confirmed that as enterprise and Ferri become bigger portions of the mix, normal consumer seasonality will be more muted going forward since the consumer business is becoming a smaller percentage of total revenue. He deferred specific Q1 and 2027 guidance to January.

Q : Can you provide an update on the Singapore arbitration? A : CFO Jason Tsai stated that closing arguments in the Singapore arbitration were held in March, and the company is still awaiting results. He declined to provide additional comments until the outcome is announced.

Q : How should we think about gross margins for the solutions business as NAND prices stabilize, and what working capital is needed to support 50%+ growth in solutions? A : CFO Jason Tsai explained that six-month pricing contracts and tight inventory turns provide margin protection. Automotive products are qualified for multi-year projects (3-5 years) with pricing and supply agreements set at the outset, supporting better margins given the solution complexity and support requirements. Regarding working capital, he stated the $1.15 billion convertible bond raise is sufficient to fund the next couple of years of business based on current forecasts, with inventory growing in Q4 before turning back into cash flow.

Q : What is Silicon Motion's strategy in China regarding NAND makers, CSPs, and competition? A : CEO Wallace Kou emphasized balancing China and the rest of the world, collaborating with YMTC directly and through module makers, and growing local China R&D to support China customers while Taiwan supports U.S. and global customers. He noted that Chinese enterprise controller companies that previously bought NAND at cyclical lows and sold drives at highs are now struggling in a non-cyclical pricing environment. Silicon Motion's strategy is to win NAND maker design wins, hyperscaler customers in both the U.S. and China, and CSPs directly, while selling controllers and firmware through module maker and NAND maker partners.

Q : How do you view the competitive landscape for enterprise controllers in China? A : CEO Wallace Kou stated that while one or two Chinese companies have moved toward IPOs, he does not see them as strong enough to compete long-term on technology or business model. He expressed confidence in Silicon Motion's position, citing its strong development pipeline for PCIe Gen 5 and Gen 6 controllers.

Q : Has the convertible bond issuance changed the dividend policy or capital structure targets? A : CFO Jason Tsai said capital allocation priorities remain unchanged: dividend, opportunistic share buybacks, and M&A as appropriate. The company recently increased its dividend to $2.30 per ADS per year and has a 10-year history of raising it. He noted working capital needs are increasing, and the convertible bond raise puts the company in a better position to drive growth with improved working capital.

Q : What is the outlook for MonTitan demand, particularly regarding HBM/DRAM innovations and KV cache requirements per GPU? A : CEO Wallace Kou said MonTitan demand comes from a wide range of customers including AI server, hyperscalers, CSPs, and the NVIDIA ecosystem. He noted compute SSD demand was larger this year due to high NAND prices, but high-capacity QLC momentum is building for next year as NAND makers ramp 2-terabit QLC production. He expects NVIDIA to redefine minimum KV cache capacity per GPU early next year, and growing KV cache demand will drive additional enterprise SSD and controller demand.

Gross margin remains below the target model, with temporary headwinds from unused capacity charges and non-recurring costs related to manufacturing reshaping.

Power and discrete segment reported an operating margin of negative 17.1%, impacted by the transition to 200mm wafers and legacy fab costs.

Input cost inflation is expected to be a headwind for gross margin, partially offsetting improvements from mix and pricing.

Q1 2027 revenue visibility is limited, with only 86 calendar days and typical seasonality, though management expects to meet consensus.

Q & A Highlights

Q : Can you clarify the timing and magnitude of the ~400 basis points of structural gross margin improvement from the manufacturing reshaping program? Will it hit all at once, and how does it fit with the path to the 44%-46% target model? A : CFO Lorenzo Grandi explained that the positive impact from reshaping the manufacturing footprint will become visible once the four legacy fabs are closed, expected toward the end of 2027 and into early 2028, and depends partly on customer qualification for three of the steps. He added that gross margin should still improve progressively each quarter from better mix, lower unused capacity charges, and reduced temporary transfer costs. Management targets the 44%-46% model and said it would update guidance in January and through next year, without committing to exceeding the target model despite strong AI-related mix.

Q : What is the outlook for the AI data center business in 2027, including the split between MCUs, silicon photonics, bipolar-CMOS and power? A : CEO Jean-Marc Chery said data center revenue will be about $1.3 billion in 2026, with more than 85% from MCUs, silicon photonics and electronic ICs, and will be "well above doubling" in 2027, with more detail to come in January. Remy Elwazan added that silicon photonics will become very relevant next year, contributing tens of percent of the total, while bipolar-CMOS wins will be mainly visible from 2028 onward, though non-negligible in 2027.

Q : What is the current backlog and visibility, and how should we think about 2027 seasonality given the shifting mix? A : Chery said book-to-bill was well above 2 overall, above 1 in every end market, and well above 3 in communication equipment/computer peripherals and industrial. Backlog is now well above $20 billion, equal to about five quarters of revenue at the Q4 midpoint, though still below the 2022-2023 peak. He noted 2027 seasonality will differ because the vertical mix is rebalancing, with automotive about 35% of revenue, industrial 22%-24%, communication/computer peripherals slightly above 20%, and personal electronics 22%, with communication/computer peripherals expected to keep growing.

Q : Can you give more color on the low Earth orbit satellite business for next year, including demand, customer base and capacity constraints? A : Remy Elwazan said 2026 was a record year for the satellite business on fast growth from the major customer, and he expects 2027 revenue to be the same or better, with additional customers ramping on top. He said ST is likely to be capacity-gated next year and is working to release more capacity, adding that its front-end module and bipolar-CMOS technologies have no close competitor given their noise-figure and spectrum-efficiency advantages.

Q : What is the outlook for automotive in 2027, including electromobility and silicon carbide? A : Chery said visibility from European Tier 1 customers has been stable for more than six months, and ST expects automotive to grow slightly above 10% for full-year 2026, roughly in line with the market. Power and discrete growth in Q4 will be well above 20%-25%, driven by European electromobility. For 2027, automotive should contribute roughly in line with the company average, while AI data centers and industrial remain the main growth drivers and consumer stays soft. Silicon carbide will grow about 20% this year and see another year of significant growth in 2027, helped by the conversion to 8-inch wafers at Catania and Shanxi.

Q : What is the status of the silicon photonics ramp in terms of yields and capacity expansion? A : Remy Elwazan said ST is ahead of plan, with customer electro-optical yields setting a new industry bar, and noted ST is the only at-scale 12-inch player shipping now, which supports critical-dimension and yield entitlement. He said the 2026 contribution is meaningful but far below next year's, when capacity will increase about 4x year on year, slightly more in practice, and described silicon photonics as a long growth story with long-term visibility.

Q : What is the direction for Q1 2027 gross margin and revenue, given the 86 calendar days in the quarter? A : Grandi said he would not formally guide Q1 gross margin but expects it to be at least at the current consensus level. Chery added that despite only 86 days in Q1, ST is comfortable delivering at least the revenue consensus for the quarter. Grandi also flagged input cost inflation as a headwind, offset by manufacturing efficiency, better mix and some price increases.

Q : What are the early indications from pricing negotiations with Tier 1 customers for next year? A : Grandi said ST is raising prices on selected products given higher input costs and longer lead times, and that if the supply-demand gap persists, 2027 pricing could be stable to slightly up. He cautioned that negotiations for next year are not yet complete, so it is too early to comment further.

Q : Was the better-than-expected personal electronics revenue in Q3 driven by a pull-in, and what does that mean for Q1? A : Chery said there was no specific pull-in; ST simply delivered customer demand, and personal electronics revenue came in better than expected, up 12% sequentially. He did not signal any risk of a Q1 payback from the Q3 strength.

Q : Why did margins decline year over year in analog/MEMS/sensors and power and discrete despite strong revenue growth, and what is the split of the 400 basis point improvement? A : Grandi said the over-400 basis point improvement combines larger wafer size, moving from poorly automated legacy fabs with high labor costs to more automated facilities, and it is complex to split the contributors. The analog/MEMS/sensors segment is suffering most in the transition phase from legacy fab transfers, with extra costs and lower efficiency, but should benefit most once production moves to the advanced 300mm fabs, while power and discrete will benefit from the move to 200mm.

Q : What is the OpEx outlook for 2027? A : Grandi said OpEx will go up next year but by less than sales, improving the operating expense-to-sales ratio.

Interested in Silicon Motion Technology Corporation? Here are five stocks we like better.

Record Q3 performance: Revenue surged 131% year over year to $560 million, beating guidance, while non-GAAP earnings per ADS rose 333% to $4.35. Growth was led by automotive Ferri products, enterprise boot drives, and SSD controllers.

3 Overlooked Tech Names Quietly Powering Everyday Life

Silicon Motion Technology (NASDAQ:SIMO) reported record third-quarter revenue and said its expanding automotive, enterprise storage and AI-related businesses are reducing its reliance on consumer device cycles.

Revenue for the September quarter rose 24% sequentially and 131% from a year earlier to $560 million, exceeding the company's guidance range of $519 million to $541 million. Non-GAAP gross margin was 53.7%, while non-GAAP earnings per ADS reached $4.35, up 79% sequentially and 333% year over year, according to CFO Jason Tsai.

"We delivered an outstanding third quarter, surpassing our expectations, driven by stronger execution and demand trends," Tsai said. The company recorded its fourth consecutive quarter of record revenue, with growth across most businesses led by Ferri automotive products, enterprise boot drives, and Edge and MonTitan SSD controllers.

Automotive and enterprise products drive mix shift

President and CEO Wallace Kou said Silicon Motion's storage solutions segment, which includes Ferri products and boot drives, produced its strongest quarterly result. Segment revenue rose more than 75% sequentially and represented more than 40% of total company revenue in the third quarter.

The company said automotive products were a particular source of strength, benefiting from its portfolio of automotive-grade storage controllers and firmware. Kou said Silicon Motion has spent more than a decade developing automotive products and certifications, and that its automotive backlog has expanded as it gains share.

Story Continues

Silicon Motion also sees opportunities to apply Ferri products in robotics, drones and advanced networking equipment. Kou said the robotics market remains at an early stage and current volumes are small, but the company is engaged with several potential customers in humanoid robots and other physical AI applications. Tsai added that automotive-grade capabilities such as tolerance for high temperatures and vibration could provide an advantage in robotics.

→ Coca-Cola Stock Is Everything AI Isn't—And That's Its Biggest Strength

Enterprise boot drives are also becoming a larger part of the company's strategy. Kou said Silicon Motion won designs with several new Tier 1 customers in networking and AI infrastructure during the third quarter. Those programs are expected to ramp over the next two years.

The company estimates the enterprise boot-drive market will be about $3 billion in 2026 and exceed $5 billion by 2030. It also identified a separate opportunity in near-CPU boot drives that use onboard DRAM, which it estimates could surpass $10 billion by 2030. Silicon Motion expects to begin ramping products for that market in the second half of 2027, subject to customer and supply-chain execution.

MonTitan enterprise controller ramp continues

Silicon Motion said its MonTitan enterprise SSD controller business is gaining traction with NAND manufacturers, hyperscalers, cloud service providers and module makers. The company said its first two customers began shipping TLC enterprise SSDs for compute applications using MonTitan controllers in the second quarter.

All seven announced customers remain on track to begin commercial ramps during 2026, according to Kou. In the near term, the company expects TLC-based compute SSDs to ramp faster than QLC-based data-storage SSDs, until broader availability of 2-terabit QLC NAND dies.

During the third quarter, Silicon Motion taped out its next-generation 4-nanometer PCIe 6 MonTitan controller. The product is intended for hyperscalers and cloud service providers, with sampling expected in the first quarter of 2027. Kou said the company has one design involving multiple Tier 1 customers, including NAND makers, hyperscalers and cloud providers.

In its Edge SSD controller business, Silicon Motion reported sequential and year-over-year growth. The company said PCIe 5 products are gaining adoption in PCs and currently account for about 10% of the PC market. Kou said the company expects PCIe 5 penetration to reach 20% to 25% by the end of 2027, supporting higher average selling prices as the market transitions from PCIe 4.

Consumer markets remain challenged

Management said higher memory and storage prices continue to pressure PC and smartphone makers, which are trying to offer affordable products amid rising NAND and DRAM costs. Silicon Motion's eMMC and UFS revenue declined modestly from the prior quarter because of customer launch timing and difficult smartphone conditions.

The company expects eMMC and UFS revenue to remain relatively flat in the near term. However, Kou said new UFS 4.1 and UFS 5 controllers could support growth next year and beyond through higher average selling prices.

While the broader consumer environment remains difficult, Silicon Motion said its increasing exposure to automotive and enterprise applications should make traditional consumer seasonality less pronounced. Tsai said consumer cycles will have less influence on results as enterprise and Ferri products become a larger part of the business.

Fourth-quarter and 2027 outlook

For the fourth quarter, Silicon Motion forecast revenue of $588 million to $616 million, representing sequential growth of 5% to 10%. Management expects growth across nearly all product segments, led by Ferri automotive products, enterprise boot-drive solutions and MonTitan enterprise controllers.

The company expects its SSD controller business to be flat to slightly lower sequentially, reflecting memory and storage market conditions and typical seasonal patterns. Silicon Motion projected fourth-quarter gross margin of 54% to 55% and operating margin of 36% to 37%.

For 2026, management said revenue is on track to more than double from the prior year and operating margin is expected to exceed 30% exiting the year. Looking ahead, Tsai said Silicon Motion expects revenue to grow by at least 40% in 2027, supported by backlog across its businesses. The company expects gross margin to remain in the low-to-mid-50% range as enterprise controllers and Ferri automotive products account for more of its mix.

Silicon Motion also highlighted its August convertible-note offering, which raised $1.15 billion in aggregate principal amount and generated $1.127 billion in net proceeds. The company ended the third quarter with $953.6 million in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash. Tsai said the capital raise is expected to fund working-capital needs for the next several years based on current forecasts, while helping the company support inventory growth and business expansion.

About Silicon Motion Technology (NASDAQ:SIMO)

Silicon Motion Technology Corporation is a fabless semiconductor company that designs, develops and markets NAND flash storage controllers. Its products manage the storage, performance, reliability and power consumption of data stored in NAND flash memory and are used in a range of consumer, mobile, computing and industrial applications.

The company's product portfolio includes controllers for solid-state drives (SSDs), embedded storage products such as eMMC and UFS devices, and other flash-based storage solutions.

What is the support that you need from an inventory perspective? Inventory already has gone up to about $800 million or so. Could you talk a little bit about how you think about how much working capital support you would need to support that kind of additional probably 50% plus growth in the solution business?

Jason Tsai: Yes. In terms of the gross margin question on the solutions business, as Wallace pointed out, we are negotiating six-month pricing contracts with our customers, and we expect to turn our inventory here within that period as well. Maintaining very tight controls around working capital and price protection and margin protection for our products and our P&L. We anticipate that, certainly with automotive, these are qualified products going into projects that are multi-year, three to five years in length. Pricing as well as supply agreements are agreed upon at the beginning of these engagements. We are confident that we can maintain better margins, especially as the solution complexity, the design, the support becomes more onerous.

Having the higher margin supports all of that. In terms of the working capital, as I said, with the raise that we have done, we are confident that we can support the next couple of years' worth of business based upon what current forecasts look like. We will continue to grow inventory, but obviously in anticipation of a 40%+ year, we have grown inventory now. We will continue to grow inventory in the next quarter, in the fourth quarter, and then we will start seeing obviously the turns of that inventory come back into cash flow as we progress.

Gokul Hariharan: Got it. Okay. Thank you.

Operator: Next question comes from the line of Daniel Yen of Morgan Stanley. Please ask your question, Daniel. Your line is open.

Daniel Yen: Yeah. Thanks, Wallace and Jason, to take my question, and congratulations on a great result. I want to switch gears to a very different question. Wallace, you just mentioned about some opportunities, for example, for your boot drive, for example, enterprise SSD. But I want to ask what will be your strategy right now in China. I think China is still the important region, and I think in China, we also have CSPs, we have NAND supplier, NAND makers. We also have a lot of module houses there. But at the same time, I think competition is still there.

So I want to consult you on Silicon Motion's strategy right now in China both with the NAND makers, with the competitors, and also how should we address maybe the future demand from the CSP in China.

Wallace Kou: Okay, you asked a very good question, Daniel. I think that we really want the balance between China and also the rest of world. China has YMTC, NAND maker, they are very strong. They grow very fast. We also support and collaborate with the YMTC directly or indirectly with the module maker. I think the enterprise portion, we see they will become stronger in 2027. I think we definitely work closely for China CSP for hyperscaler. Believe us, and I think that is why we try to grow China local R&D. Eventually, we want China, our local R&D can support China customer. In Taiwan, we support the rest of world, especially for U.S. customers.

Secondly, I think the China, they are growing enterprise controller company, but in the past, they also like to make enterprise C drive. In the past, as you know, NAND pricing is cyclical. They have a downside, they have upside. So some enterprise controller company, they buy the NAND in the downside, they are selling the drive in the upside. But nowadays, there is no longer the cyclical price going up or stable, right? So very hard for enterprise controller company, you use it converting to selling the whole solution if you do not win hyperscaler or even NAND maker of the CSP customer. So I think our strategy is very simple. We winning NAND maker business and designing directly.

We win hyperscaler customer in both U.S. and China. We also win CSP directly. But we do not make enterprise solution. We only sell controller and our firmware. We enable the module maker and the NAND maker. They sell and utilize our controller and the firmware, make enterprise solution, and selling to the customer. So this is where we are. That is why building Silicon Motion ecosystem, working together and supporting the growing opportunity in both China and U.S.

Daniel Yen: I see. Very clear. Wallace, if I may follow up, how should we think about the overall competitive landscape on a controller in China right now? Just want to get your opinion.

Wallace Kou: For enterprise, we really do not even. There is one or two basic company move to the IPO, but we do not see they are strong enough to compete in the long term, not just one technology or business model, right? I do not really see any threat from them. Even some also want to go overseas. Today, we feel pretty comfortable for our position and with our technology, and we have a very strong developing pipeline for both our PCIe Gen 5 as well as Gen 6.

Daniel Yen: I see. Yes. Thanks for this. The second question from me is that since right now I think you are issuing the convertible bond, I want to ask if there is any change on your dividend policy potentially in the future? Also I think just overall, how should we think about your capital structure going forward? Do you have a target, any ratio you are looking at? I think this question is actually coming from some of the investors who subscribe your convertible bond. Thank you.

Jason Tsai: Yeah. Dividend and capital allocation certainly continues to be a priority. We increased our dividend a couple of weeks ago from $2-$2.30 per ADS per year. We have had a history of increasing our dividend over the last 10 years or so, and our expectation is that we can continue to look at that strategically over time and continue to look at opportunities to raise that. The three priorities for us on capital return is dividend, share buybacks opportunistically, and then M&A as it makes sense, and that is unchanged. But certainly right now, working capital needs continue to increase as well.

The CB raise puts us in a much better position to drive growth in our business with better working capital as well.

Daniel Yen: Thank you, Jason. That is all my questions. Thank you.

Operator: Thank you. We have now reached the end of the question and answer session. I will now turn the conference back to Mr. Wallace Kou for closing comments.

Wallace Kou: Thank you everyone for joining us today and for your continuing interest in Silicon Motion. We will be attending several investor conferences over the next few months. The schedule of these events will be posted on the investor relationship section of our corporate website, and we look forward to speaking with you at these events. Goodbye for now.

Okta Rides on Strong Enterprise Demand & New Products

Okta is well-positioned to benefit from increasing enterprise investments in identity security as organizations accelerate AI adoption and modernize their cybersecurity infrastructure. The proliferation of autonomous AI agents across applications, cloud platforms and enterprise systems is creating demand for identity discovery, authentication, access controls and governance. Okta for AI Agents enables enterprises to discover, secure and govern AI agents while enforcing access policies across heterogeneous environments. Growing adoption of agentic AI is expected to expand the company's addressable market and create additional cross-selling opportunities across its identity security portfolio.

Okta's newer offerings, including Okta Identity Governance, Okta Privileged Access, Identity Security Posture Management, Identity Threat Protection and Okta for AI Agents, are helping customers address increasingly complex security requirements. Deals involving newer products generated an average annual contract value (ACV) uplift of approximately 40%, highlighting significant cross-selling and upselling opportunities. Okta is benefiting from solid demand among large enterprises, improving sales productivity and strong customer expansion activity. news.Title: Arista Networks (ANET) vs. CSCO and AVGO: Is AI Data Center Expansion Creating a Long-Term Networking Winner?
news.Content:
Is ANET a good stock to buy? We came across a bullish thesis on Arista Networks, Inc. on TradersPro's Substack. Since the thesis was published on August 29th, ANET shares have pulled back amid profit-taking and valuation concerns after a strong rally, creating a near-term pause while AI networking demand continues to support the longer-term growth case. In this article, we will summarize the bulls' thesis on ANET. Arista Networks, Inc.'s share was trading at $186.72 as of October 28th 2026. ANET's trailing and forward P/E were 55.91 and 33.82 respectively according to Yahoo Finance.

This isn't the first time we see a networking equipment company pitched as a great investment. ANET shares gained 42.50% year to date. Comparable technology stocks like Cisco Systems and NVIDIA gained 43.18% and 15.49%, respectively, during the same period. Why are AI infrastructure stocks rising so much and is it really a good time to buy them?

In May, we published an article about the 10 Stocks That Will Make You Rich Over the Next Decade and ANET ranked #4 in that article. ANET returned 31.76% since then. So, hedge funds were right about ANET. This article highlights ANET among the 12 Best NYSE Stocks to Buy for Long-Term Investment. Before getting into our analysis, let's take a look at the business and why some investors like the stock so much.

Arista Networks, Inc. (NASDAQ:ANET) makes the networking equipment that connects servers, data centers, and enterprise systems, using high-speed switches, routers, and its EOS software. Its biggest growth opportunity right now is AI infrastructure, where massive AI computing clusters need faster, more reliable connections between chips, making Arista Networks, Inc. a key supplier of the "plumbing" behind the AI boom.

Read More: 15 AI Stocks That Are Quietly Making Investors Rich

Read More: Undervalued AI Stock Poised For Massive Gains: 10000% Upside Potential

The company is also benefiting from steady spending by large cloud providers, growing demand for office and campus networking, expansion into routers, and a large existing customer base that keeps generating repeat business. Investors are watching closely because AI infrastructure still can't keep up with AI demand, and that gap is where Arista Networks, Inc. sees its opportunity ( see how Arista's $6.9 billion in deferred revenue relates to its cash flow ).

The bullish argument is simple: as AI systems get more powerful, they need more bandwidth and faster connections. This lets Arista Networks, Inc. grow along two paths at once — more AI clusters being built overall, and each cluster needing better networking gear than the last. Its core switching business is well placed for this, while its newer push into routers and campus networks adds growth beyond just AI data centers.

Story Continues

A key part of the long-term story is the shift toward liquid-cooled AI infrastructure, which changes how high-density data centers are built. As AI servers use more power and generate more heat, traditional cooling starts to fall short, forcing new approaches to layout, power delivery, and system design. If this shift continues, Arista Networks, Inc. could play a bigger role in connecting these next-generation systems, though it still has to prove it can turn this opportunity into consistent growth.

The main risk is a slowdown in AI spending or delays in data center buildouts by large customers. Networking demand depends heavily on this spending, and factors like component shortages, tariffs, power limits, and the sheer complexity of liquid-cooled builds could all slow things down. The market already expects a lot from Arista Networks, Inc., so continuing to win AI networking deals matters more than ever — any stumble in adoption of its newer platforms could weigh on the stock.

Another risk for the stock is that AI networking growth benefits competing technologies more than Arista's Ethernet platforms. Rising spending on AI clusters does not guarantee that customers will choose Arista's equipment. Its annual report identifies InfiniBand and NVLink as competing technologies, often sold alongside NVIDIA's graphics processors as integrated solutions. Customers choosing these packages could leave less networking business available to independent suppliers. Arista might then need to offer lower prices or spend more on development to win deployments. That would put pressure on margins even if overall AI infrastructure investment remains strong. In our opinion, the stock's premium becomes harder to justify if the networking market expands faster than Arista's ability to capture profitable orders.

Beyond AI, growth in campus networking, routing products, and support revenue from its installed base gives the company other ways to grow, so it isn't fully dependent on one market. Still, how fast AI-related demand keeps growing will be the biggest factor in whether the stock's current optimism is justified.

The stock's momentum has picked up recently, with trading volume rising and the stock moving into a stronger technical position — a sign of growing investor confidence. But the longer-term outlook still hinges on whether AI spending keeps converting into real networking orders, and whether growth holds up as expectations climb. A slowdown in AI infrastructure spending or delays from big customers could pressure the stock even if the broader industry keeps growing.

AI remains the main reason investors are bullish, but there's a risk that demand stays concentrated among just a handful of large cloud customers. If those customers keep expanding their AI clusters and adopting newer, denser computing setups, Arista Networks, Inc. should keep benefiting. The real test is whether this turns into lasting earnings growth rather than a short-term spending wave.

Hedge fund positioning shows a mixed but generally constructive signal. As per our database, 91 hedge fund portfolios held Arista Networks, Inc. at the end of the second quarter, up from 85 in the previous quarter. This increase suggests institutional interest in the stock strengthened, supporting its appeal as an AI infrastructure investment. By comparison, Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO) was held by 101 hedge funds, up from 97, NVIDIA was held by 285 hedge funds, up from 275, and Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) was held by 170 hedge funds, down from 173. NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) stood out with the strongest increase in hedge fund interest by number of funds, followed by Arista Networks and Cisco Systems, while Broadcom saw a modest pullback, suggesting institutional enthusiasm remained broadly positive across the group.

Short interest data also paints a fairly calm picture for Arista Networks, Inc. relative to its peers. About 1.17% of Arista Networks, Inc.'s float is sold short, almost identical to Broadcom Inc. at 1.14%, but below NVIDIA Corporation at 1.30% and Cisco Systems, Inc. at 1.53%. This suggests Arista Networks, Inc. is drawing similarly limited skepticism to Broadcom Inc., with bearish bets remaining low across all four AI infrastructure companies.

Valuation Analysis

ANET's forward P/E is 33.82x. Broadcom Inc., Cisco Systems, Inc., and NVIDIA Corporation trade at forward P/Es of 18.25x, 20.53x, and 13.79x, respectively. ANET's own forward P/E was 32.75x on December 31, 2025, making its current multiple approximately 3% higher. We believe the current valuation reflects strong investor expectations for AI networking demand, continued cloud spending, and expansion into campus networking and routing. However, the premium appears demanding despite Arista's strong profitability and earnings growth, as its multiple exceeds all three peers. Arista's revenue increased 37.7% to $3.04 billion in the second quarter of 2026, while net income rose approximately 36% to $1.21 billion, demonstrating that increased demand is translating into substantial earnings. We believe ANET can justify its current valuation without accelerating beyond this growth rate if strong earnings growth persists and margins remain resilient. If Arista maintains its Ethernet leadership and successfully converts AI investment into sustained earnings growth, its premium could remain justified, but we would wait for a lower entry price given the limited room for disappointment.

Previously, we covered a bullish thesis on Arista Networks Inc (ANET) by Charly AI in April 2025, which highlighted the AI and cloud networking growth, strong margins, balance sheet strength, and long-term upside despite near-term pressures. ANET's stock price has appreciated by approximately 168.66% since our coverage. We believe ANET could offer an attractive entry point at a lower valuation if AI networking demand sustains earnings growth and Arista preserves its margins, despite its premium multiple and competition from integrated alternatives.

Arista Networks is not on our list of the 40 Most Popular Stocks Among Hedge Funds . While ANET could offer long-term upside if it converts AI networking demand into sustained earnings growth, we believe some AI stocks offer stronger long-term potential at more attractive valuations, with a high probability of delivering superior returns on a much shorter timeline. If you are looking for an AI stock that is more promising than ANET and that has 10,000% upside potential, check out our report about this cheapest AI stock .

news.Title: 3 Stocks to Consider From a Flourishing Networking Industry
news.Content:
The Zacks Computer - Networking industry participants are expected to benefit from the networking infrastructure upgrade driven by AI workloads, cloud computing, big data, network security and next-generation connectivity.

The proliferation of AI workloads and hyperscale data centers is accelerating investments in high-speed interconnects, optical networking and Ethernet switches. Players in this space are focused on capitalizing on the multi-billion-dollar AI infrastructure opportunity. Increasing adoption of AI-driven applications across enterprises is also driving investments in next-gen networking infrastructure capable of supporting higher bandwidth, lower latency and heightened security requirements. Continued deployment of 5G, the proliferation of the Internet of Things (IoT), industrial automation and edge computing is strengthening demand for reliable connectivity solutions. Increasing deployment of Wi-Fi 7 also presents a significant growth opportunity.

Also, the explosion of AI workloads requires a major upgrade to observability infrastructure. There is a greater need for continuous monitoring of hybrid environments and tighter security amid rising attacks. This will spur demand for innovative networking products, favoring prospects for prominent industry players such as Cisco Systems CSCO, Digi International DGII and Lantronix LTRX.

However, cautious IT spending amid heightened uncertainty over global macroeconomic conditions and volatile supply-chain dynamics due to tariff troubles continues to be concerning for the participants in the near term. Fierce competition is an overhang on pricing power and margin expansion.

Industry Description

The Zacks Computer-Networking industry comprises companies that offer networking and Internet-connected products, including wireless (Wi-Fi and Long-Term Evolution or LTE), Ethernet and powerline, focusing on dependability and ease of use. The products are available in numerous configurations to cater to the changing requirements of consumers in each geographic territory where it operates. Several industry players also provide mission-critical IoT solutions and network security services to help clients build next-generation connected products, and implement and manage critical communications infrastructures in demanding environments with enhanced safety levels. Focus on developing IoT sensors, drones and wearables amid increasing demand for cloud computing-based contact tracing applications is driving the industry.

Story Continues

4 Trends Influencing the Industry's Future

Technological Advancement Opening Business Avenues: The proliferation of generative AI, agentic AI and high adoption of cloud and data-intensive applications is driving higher traffic and creating a need for advanced optical networking, high-speed interconnects, Ethernet switches, routing and wireless infrastructure. The transition toward 800G and 1.6T networking technologies is expected to further drive infrastructure modernization and capacity expansion.

Expansion of industrial IoT and edge computing, and the increasing popularity of smart connected devices are further creating growth opportunities. Rising cybersecurity concerns are emerging as a key tailwind, driving demand for solutions such as threat detection, network monitoring and zero-trust security architectures.

Continued Deployment of 5G to Boost Growth Prospects: The continued expansion of the 5G technology hinges on substantial investments to upgrade infrastructure in the core fiber backhaul network to support growth in data services. Efforts to develop smart connected homes, hospitals, factories, buildings, cities and self-driving vehicles bode well for industry players. These firms invest heavily in LTE, broadband and fiber to provide additional capacity and improve Internet and wireless networks. These initiatives hold promise.

Wi-Fi 7 Upgrade Cycle to Drive Momentum: Brisk technological advancement, dynamic products, high-speed connectivity, low latency and evolving industry standards define the networking industry. The growing clout of the latest Wi-Fi 6E-compliant residential gateways, Wi-Fi routers, set-top boxes and wireless range extenders is a testament to the same. The increasing demand for connecting more devices to the network has been driving demand for Wi-Fi 6E devices. Wi-Fi 6E addresses Wi-Fi spectrum shortage issues by providing continuous channel bandwidth to support a higher number of connected devices without compromising speed. The rollout of Wi-Fi 7 bodes well for the companies in this space.

Macroeconomic Turmoil Is Concerning: Global macroeconomic weakness and volatile supply-chain dynamics are persistent concerns. Tariff troubles, especially between the United States and China, remain an overhang on global supply chains. Inflation could affect spending across small and medium-sized businesses globally and uncertainty in business visibility could dent the industry's near-term performance.

The computer networking industry remains highly competitive, with a large number of established and new players vying for market share. As growth stabilizes, competition often intensifies, leading to pricing pressure and margin compression.

Zacks Industry Rank Indicates Bright Near-Term Prospects

The Zacks Computer-Networking Industry is housed within the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector. The industry carries a Zacks Industry Rank #75, positioning it in the top 30% of more than 247 Zacks industries.

The group's Zacks Industry Rank, which is the average of the Zacks Rank of all the member stocks, indicates bright near-term prospects. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than two to one.

Before we present a few stocks you may want to consider for your portfolio, considering bright prospects, let us look at the industry's recent stock-market performance and valuation picture

Industry Outperforms the S&P 500 and the Sector

The Zacks Computer-Networking industry has outperformed the S&P 500 composite and the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector in the past year.

The industry has gained 51.9% over this period, compared with the broader sector's 13.4% rally. The S&P 500 has appreciated 13.3% over the same time frame.

One-Year Price Performance

Industry's Current Valuation

Based on the forward 12-month price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio, a common multiple for valuing Computer-Networking stocks, the industry is currently trading at 24.62X, compared with the S&P 500's 19.27X. It is also higher than the sector's forward-12-month P/E of 19.25X.

In the past five years, the industry traded as high as 31.47X and as low as 12.45X, with the median being 17.27X, as the charts below show.

3 Computer-Networking Stocks to Add to Your Portfolio

Cisco Systems: Headquartered in San Jose, CA, the company offers identity and access, advanced threat and unified threat management solutions.

Cisco is benefiting from the demand for AI Infrastructure solutions, with hyperscaler demand acting as a key catalyst. The company expects AI infrastructure revenues from hyperscalers to reach $7.5 billion in fiscal 2027.

Strong demand for its Silicon One based systems and Acacia optical networking solutions is expected to support growth. Fiscal 2026 hyperscaler AI orders were about 60% Silicon One-based systems and 40% optics. Acacia generated more than $1 billion in orders in the fiscal fourth quarter.

On the last earnings call, CSCO noted that accelerating agentic AI is driving a "networking super cycle" resulting in increasing demand for its Networking stack to support inferencing across cloud, on-premise and edge environments. In October, Cisco announced a collaboration with NVIDIA to develop an open industry specification for next-generation 400G-per-lane pluggable optics, further strengthening its position in the evolving AI networking ecosystem.

For fiscal 2027, Cisco projects revenues of $72.2-$73.4 billion and non-GAAP earnings of $5.05-$5.11 per share. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fiscal 2027 bottom line is pinned at $5.11, unchanged in the past 30 days. Shares have gained 51.3% in the past year.

At present, CSCO carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

Price & Consensus: CSCO

Lantronix : Based in Irvine, CA, Lantronix specializes in providing Industrial and Edge AI IoT solutions for high-growth applications in certain verticals, including enterprise IT, smart cities and commercial and defense unmanned systems.

The company's unmanned systems business has emerged as a meaningful growth driver. Revenues from Unmanned systems came in at $12.6 million in fiscal 2026 and management expects the segment to represent 15% to 20% of total revenues in fiscal 2027. Increasing adoption of AI-enabled drones and counter-UAS applications across defense, industrial and commercial applications presents significant opportunities for its unmanned systems business. The recent inclusion of its Open-Q 8550CS system-on-module in the Blue UAS Framework strengthens its ability to serve U.S. defense drone manufacturers.

The company also introduced the Spotter edge AI computing platform, which expands its offerings for autonomous drones and robotics.

Beyond unmanned systems, the IoT System Solutions is witnessing improving conditions after federal government shutdowns led to extended procurement cycles. The tuck-in acquisition of Vecima Networks' Industrial IoT business, including the Nero Global Tracking platform, is also expanding its recurring software revenue base.

However, tightening memory availability and rising costs remain concerns, while the increasing contribution from relatively lower-margin unmanned systems solutions could weigh on profitability.

At present, LTRX carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fiscal 2027 earnings is 22 cents per share, unchanged in the past 60 days. Shares have gained 23.8% in the past year.

Price & Consensus: LTRX

Digi International: Based in Hopkins, MN, Digi is a well-known provider of business and mission-critical Internet of Things (IoT) products and services globally. The company's industrial Internet of Things offerings encompass embedded, edge and turnkey vertical solutions. These solutions find applications across emerging technology trends such as AI, edge computing and industrial automation. The company is embedding AI across its portfolio.

Digi's outlook remains supported by sustained ARR growth, ongoing benefits from acquisitions and the long-term opportunity to integrate AI into industrial IoT solutions. The company expects ARR to grow 27% in fiscal 2026, up from 25% projected earlier.

To capitalize on the AI opportunity, DGII had unveiled DANI, the Digi Artificial Network Intelligence agent, earlier in the year. DANI is an AI network operations agent that is embedded in Digi Remote Manager, a networking device management platform, enabling network operators/managed service providers to monitor issues, identify causes and offer recommended actions through a unified conversational interface.

The recent launch of Digi EX60, an enterprise 5G router integrating Wi-Fi 7 and AI-assisted network management capabilities, further strengthens its offerings for distributed enterprise networks.

Digi continues to pursue strategic acquisitions, which are likely to supplement organic growth. The proposed acquisition of Disruptive Technologies is expected to expand the capabilities and reach of its SmartSense platform. The company expects the transaction to contribute approximately $9 million in additional adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow in fiscal 2028. The transaction is expected to close before the end of 2026, subject to regulatory approval.

On the last earnings call, management highlighted challenges in the supply chain, which could exert pressure on margins.

At present, DGII carries a Zacks Rank #3. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fiscal 2027 bottom line is pegged at $3.17, unchanged in the past 60 days. Shares have gained 106% in the past year.

Price & Consensus: DGII
